question.text: Which of the following legal documents, per Ch 12, is NORMALLY SIGNED AT THE TIME OF INVESTING IN AN OFFSHORE FUND (as distinct from an onshore Indian AIF)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 12 explicitly: 'The Subscription Agreement is signed at the time of investing in Offshore Funds, while a Contribution Agreement is signed at the time of investing in Onshore Funds.' The Trap: A is the ONSHORE variant. B is the trust-formation document. C is between the Fund and the Manager, not LP. Cross-Exam Context: This onshore/offshore split recurs when discussing GIFT IFSC AIFs. In XIX-C Managers of GIFT-based funds must get this right. Manager's Pro-Tip: If you run a parallel GIFT-IFSC vehicle alongside an onshore Cat II fund, use consistent economic terms in both. Side-by-side Subscription and Contribution Agreements should mirror each other's carry waterfall.
